title: The tensor product of sheaves is closed and right exact
statement:
In the situation of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure], for sheaves $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ put
$\mathcal{H}om(\mathcal F,\mathcal G):=[\mathcal F,\mathcal G]$, the presheaf internal hom of
[det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf], which is a sheaf by [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-hom-sheaf].
Then there are bijections
$$
\Hom_{\Sh}(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G,\mathcal H)\cong\Hom_{\Sh}\bigl(\mathcal G,\mathcal{H}om(\mathcal F,\mathcal H)\bigr),
$$
natural in all three variables. Hence $(\Sh(C,\mathcal A),\otimes)$ is closed symmetric monoidal,
and $\mathcal F\otimes-$ and $-\otimes\mathcal F$ preserve all colimits; in particular they are
additive and right exact.

proof.text: Write $\iota$ for the inclusion of sheaves into presheaves and $a$ for sheafification. For fixed $\mathcal F$, the presheaf functor $[\iota\mathcal F,-]$ takes $\iota\mathcal H$ to a sheaf by [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-hom-sheaf]. Its maps are the internal-hom maps of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf]; since the sheaf category is full, these maps are also sheaf morphisms. Thus $Q_{\mathcal F}(\mathcal H)=[\iota\mathcal F,\iota\mathcal H]$ defines a sheaf-valued functor. The same construction is contravariantly functorial in $\mathcal F$.

source.place: Statement: internal hom into a sheaf is a sheaf

proof.text:
For sheaves $\mathcal F,\mathcal G,\mathcal H$, the definition of the tensor product in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure], the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and the adjunction stated in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf] give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sh}}(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G,\mathcal H)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sh}}(a(\iota\mathcal F\otimes_p \iota\mathcal G),\mathcal H)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PSh}}(\iota\mathcal F\otimes_p \iota\mathcal G,\iota\mathcal H)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PSh}}(\iota\mathcal G,[\iota\mathcal F,\iota\mathcal H])
=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sh}}(\mathcal G,Q_{\mathcal F}\mathcal H).$$
The last equality uses fullness and [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-hom-sheaf]. The two adjunction bijections are natural, and the first and last identifications simply retain the same underlying morphisms. Their composite is therefore natural in all three variables, including the contravariant variable $\mathcal F$. This is the required adjunction $\mathcal F\otimes-\dashv Q_{\mathcal F}$. Together with the symmetric monoidal structure already given in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure], it proves closed symmetric monoidality with the specified internal hom.

source.place: Statement: displayed tensor-hom bijection and closedness clause; explicit adjunction argument

proof.text: All colimits here are small in the coefficient universe, with the size convention on $C$ of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf]. The hypothesis that $\mathcal A$ is Grothendieck abelian supplies small colimits by [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. For a small sheaf diagram $D:I\to\mathrm{Sh}(C,\mathcal A)$, form the presheaf $P$ with $P(U)=\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}(\iota D_i)(U)$; its restriction maps are induced uniquely by the restriction maps of the diagram. For each presheaf $T$, a map $P\to T$ is exactly a compatible family $\iota D_i\to T$: the objectwise colimit property gives the components, and their naturality follows by uniqueness after precomposition with every colimit map. By [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], maps $aP\to\mathcal H$ are therefore exactly compatible sheaf maps $D_i\to\mathcal H$. This is the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], so $aP$ is the colimit of $D$. This also applies to the empty diagram and to every finite diagram.

source.place: Definition 002F (definition-colimit), universal property; elementary application of sheafification

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to the adjunction of step 2. It proves that $\mathcal F\otimes-$ preserves every small colimit constructed in step 3. The symmetry from [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure] also gives a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sh}}(\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal F,\mathcal H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sh}}(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G,\mathcal H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sh}}(\mathcal G,Q_{\mathcal F}\mathcal H),$$
where the first map is precomposition with the symmetry $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G\to\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal F$. Hence $-\otimes\mathcal F$ is also left adjoint to $Q_{\mathcal F}$ and the same cited theorem proves preservation of every small colimit for it.

source.place: Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact, part (1) and its proof

proof.text: The sheaf category is additive, as needed for the last clause. Indeed, the abelian-category hypothesis on $\mathcal A$ in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf] supplies the structures listed in [def-sp-abelian]. Sums and negatives of sheaf morphisms are taken componentwise and remain natural because composition in $\mathcal A$ is bilinear. The zero presheaf is a sheaf. The pointwise biproduct $B(U)=\mathcal G(U)\oplus\mathcal H(U)$ is also a sheaf: for any test object $A\in\mathcal A$, maps $A\to B(U)$ are pairs of maps to the two factors; matching pairs glue uniquely coordinate by coordinate because $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal H$ are sheaves. The pointwise inclusions and projections are natural and satisfy $p_ri_s=\delta_{rs}$ and $i_1p_1+i_2p_2=1$. They are thus a biproduct in the sense of [def-weil-additive-category].

source.place: Section Additive categories: pointwise verification of zero object, preadditivity and biproduct identities

proof.text:
Let $T$ be either tensor functor. Step 4 says that $T$ preserves zero objects and binary coproducts. Under the canonical coproduct identification $T(X\oplus Y)\cong T(X)\oplus T(Y)$, it carries inclusions to inclusions. A zero morphism factors through the zero object, so $T(0)=0$ on morphisms; consequently it carries the projections to projections as well, by their compositions with the two inclusions. It then carries diagonals to diagonals, codiagonals to codiagonals, and $f\oplus g$ to $T(f)\oplus T(g)$, by these same component identities. Applying $T$ to
$$f+g=\nabla_Y\circ(f\oplus g)\circ\Delta_X$$
therefore gives $T(f+g)=T(f)+T(g)$, exactly additivity as defined in [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. Finally every finite diagram is a small diagram, so step 4 says that $T$ preserves all finite colimits. This is right exactness (Stacks Tag 0034, definition-exact), including preservation of cokernels. Thus both tensor functors are additive and right exact.
